Subject: In every completed 500-day window, Bitcoin closed below the entry price

One number from a daily-close archive that starts in July 2011: across every completed 500-day window around a Bitcoin halving, price closed a median 11.7% below the 500-days-before entry at some point before the halving itself. The 2012 window is the outlier on the deep side, and the page publishes each window's lowest close and the date it happened, plus a test of what moving the entry date 30, 60 and 120 days earlier or later did to the exit multiple. Everything is computed from the same archive, daily closes only, and it is free to cite.

The table and the method are here: https://btc500.net/bitcoin-500-day-cycle

owner_asks.content:
Topic title: I tested the 500-day halving rule with the entry moved 120 days earlier. It was worse every time.

I keep a daily-close archive back to July 2011 and use it to test one fixed rule: buy 500 days before the halving, sell 500 days after.

The obvious objection is that 500 is an arbitrary round number, so I re-ran every completed window with the exit fixed at the same 500-days-after date and the entry moved from 120 days earlier to 120 days later.

Moving the entry 120 days earlier made the exit multiple worse in 3 of 3 windows where the archive covers the earlier date, median -32.5%. Moving it later was mixed: small gains in some windows, worse in others, and the 2012 window distorts any average because the archive begins exactly at its entry.

The full table (per window, per offset), the drawdown record and the method are here: https://btc500.net/bitcoin-500-day-cycle

Caveat worth stating in the thread: this is four completed windows of daily closes, so it is a description of the past, not a forecast, and intraday lows were deeper than the close data shows.
